title: Personal Checking: which extended overdraft fee a bank-error review concerns
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to the bank-error review of an extended overdraft fee on a Personal Checking account. It fixes which fee is reviewed and what its posting date says about the negative episode it was charged on.

## Formal clauses

1. **The fee presupposes an episode.** An extended overdraft fee presupposes a negative episode, and it posts the tier's extended overdraft trigger period, in calendar days, after the negative-since date, the day the episode began.
2. **Which fee.** This review concerns the account's most recently posted extended overdraft fee. Any earlier one is reviewed under the general Personal Checking fee refund rules.

## Reading the posting date (derived)

Because the fee posts the trigger period after the day the episode began, counting back the trigger period in calendar days from the reviewed fee's posting date gives the day that episode began.

| Hypothetical trigger period | Reviewed fee posted on | Episode began on |
|---|---|---|
| 10 calendar days | 2026-07-21 | 2026-07-11 |
| 10 calendar days | 2026-08-03 | 2026-07-24 |

(The trigger period of 10 days is chosen only for illustration.)

## Worked case (hypothetical)

An account shows extended overdraft fees posted on 2026-02-14 and on 2026-07-21. The fee of 2026-07-21 is the most recently posted and is the one under this review; the fee of 2026-02-14 is reviewed under the general fee refund rules.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "the extended overdraft fee posts on the day the balance first went negative". **Correct basis:** it posts the trigger period after that day.
- **Wrong reading:** "all extended overdraft fees on the account are reviewed together here". **Correct basis:** only the most recently posted one is; earlier ones go under the general fee refund rules.
